title: Aug 19 Results + Aug 20 Preview: Sixty Percent Never Felt So Good
summary: 9-6 on Aug 19 with solid pitching reads, plus tomorrow's Cardinals-Reds rematch

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About Winning Days

Sixty percent. That's the number that matters when you're playing the long game in baseball predictions. And on August 19th, our model delivered exactly that—a solid 9-6 performance that reminds us why we trust the process even when a few close calls don't go our way.

## The Wins That Stood Out

The Rays continue to be one of those teams where our model just *gets* them. That 61% confidence pick? Money. Same story with the Twins hosting the Braves—another 61% call that landed perfectly. And let's talk about the White Sox-Cubs crosstown matchup, where we leaned Sox at 58% and watched them deliver.

The Phillies taking care of business against the Marlins at 60% confidence was the kind of steady pick that builds winning days. Even the Pirates squeaking past the Tigers at just 53% showed that sometimes the model sees something the rest of us don't.

## The Ones That Got Away

Look, nobody bats 1.000 in this game. The Padres-Mets miss at 61% stung a little—that's the kind of confidence level where you expect to cash. The Guardians falling to the Giants despite our 61% lean was another head-scratcher. And that Cardinals loss to the Reds? Well, here's where it gets interesting, because we're going right back to that well tomorrow.

The Orioles-Yankees toss-up at 50-50 went the other way, but that's why it was a coin flip. The Red Sox stumbling against the Diamondbacks rounded out our misses, but nothing here suggests the model was wildly off—just baseball being baseball.

## Tomorrow's Redemption Story

Here's what I love about baseball: you always get another chance. The Cardinals dropped that game to the Reds yesterday despite our 57% confidence, but tomorrow we're riding with St. Louis again—this time at 61%.

Michael McGreevy gets the ball for the Cardinals against Brady Singer and the Reds. The model sees something in this pitching matchup that it likes even more than yesterday's setup. Maybe it's McGreevy's recent form, maybe it's how the Cardinals' lineup matches up against Singer's repertoire, or maybe it's just the baseball gods balancing the scales.

## The Bottom Line

A 60% hit rate is exactly where we want to be—profitable, sustainable, and proof that the model's doing its job. We took our lumps on a few high-confidence misses, but we also cashed plenty of tickets when it mattered.

Tomorrow brings a fresh slate and a chance to run it back with the Cardinals. Sometimes the best picks are the ones where you get a second bite at the apple. Let's see if St. Louis can flip the script.

*Trust the numbers. Ride the wave. See you tomorrow.*
